request.description: Requires login. Returns one page of the trips the logged-in user created, sorted by start date by default: `content`, `page`, `size`, `totalElements` and `last` (true on the last page). `sort` accepts `id`, `name`, `destination`, `startDate`, `endDate` and `createdAt` (for example `sort=name,desc`); another property is a 400. 401 without a session.

response.name: First page
response.body:
{
  "content": [
    {
      "id": 12,
      "creatorId": 7,
      "name": "Lisbon getaway",
      "destination": "Lisbon",
      "startDate": "2027-05-01",
      "endDate": "2027-05-05",
      "budget": 1200.5,
      "description": "Pasteis de nata and trams",
      "coverImageId": null
    }
  ],
  "page": 0,
  "size": 10,
  "totalElements": 1,
  "last": true
}

request.description: Only the creator. `coverImageId` is null without cover; otherwise the picture is at `GET /api/v1/images/{coverImageId}`. 400 for an id that is not a number, 401, 403 for another user's trip and 404 for a trip that does not exist.

request.description: The logged-in user becomes the creator. Dates are `yyyy-MM-dd`; the end must not be before the start (the same day is a one-day trip). `name` and `destination` are required (up to 100 characters); `budget` (up to 2 decimals, not negative) and `description` (up to 2000 characters) are optional. Answers 201 with `Location`, 400 or 401. The cover is set afterwards with `PUT /api/v1/trips/{id}/cover`.

request.description: Only the creator. Deletes the trip together with its cover image. 204, 400, 401, 403 or 404.

Only the creator. Uploads the cover in the `file` part: JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB. Answers 201 with `Location` the first time and 200 when it replaces the previous cover (which is deleted), 400 for a file that is not a valid image, 401, 403, 404 and 413 for a file that is too large.

  "timestamp": "2026-10-25T10:00:00Z",
  "status": 400,
  "error": "Bad Request",
  "message": "Only JPEG, PNG and WebP images are accepted",
  "path": "/api/v1/trips/12/cover"
}

request.description: Only the creator. Returns the bytes of the cover with its `Content-Type` and `Cache-Control: no-cache`. 404 when the trip does not exist or has no cover (the web application then shows its default image). The web application reads covers through the public `GET /api/v1/images/{coverImageId}`.
Only the creator. Deletes the cover image. Also answers 204 when there was no cover. 401, 403 or 404.

Registers a regular user (public). Answers 201 with a Location header and the user without the password, 400 for invalid data and 409 if the email is already registered. It does not log in: call Login afterwards.

Logs in with email and password. The response sets the HttpOnly `AuthToken` cookie, which Postman stores and sends in later requests. The default development administrator is admin@tripmate.com / admin.

header.value: AuthToken=<jwt>; Path=/api; Max-Age=86400; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

request.description: Requires being logged in as that user. Answers 200 with the profile (never the password; `avatarId` is null without avatar), 401 if not logged in, 403 for another user's profile and 404 if the user does not exist. Replace 7 with the `id` returned by Login.

  "status": 403,

  "message": "Only the user can access their own profile",

request.description: Edits the name and email of one's own profile (same rules as registration; the email is stored in lower case). The session stays open after an email change. Answers 200 with the profile, 400 for invalid data, 401, 403 (another user, or the administrator, whose details come from the configuration), 404 and 409 if the email is already registered.

Changes one's own password. Requires the current password; the new one has 8 to 72 characters. Answers 204, 400 (invalid new password or incorrect current password), 401, 403 (another user, or the administrator) and 404. Sessions already open stay valid until their token expires.

Uploads the avatar of one's own profile in the `file` part: JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB. Answers 201 with `Location` the first time and 200 when it replaces the previous avatar (which is deleted), 400 for a file that is not a valid image, 401, 403, 404 and 413 for a file that is too large. The administrator can also change their avatar.

}

request.description: Returns the bytes of the user's avatar with its `Content-Type` and `Cache-Control: no-cache`. Any logged-in user can read it. Answers 404 if the user does not exist or has no avatar. The application shows avatars with `GET /api/v1/images/{avatarId}` instead, which can be cached.
Deletes one's own avatar and its image. Answers 204 also when there was none, 401, 403 and 404.
Requires being logged in. Send the picture in the `file` part: JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB. The `Location` header has the URL to read it.
